recent.text: Yes. It is, quite literally, this simple. They're rebuilding and have been rebuilding regardless of what happens with the Big Three and regardless of their playoff berth last season. They're trying to minimize the post-Crosby window of non-competitiveness as much as possible.
recent.author: Kelsey Surmacz
recent.quoted_text: Kyle Dubas has two jobs: 1. Give the Big Three a dignified exit, whenever and however that happens. Almost completely out of his control. 2. Make surethe Penguins have a baseline of competitive young NHLers so the transition post-Crosby isn't a Blackhawks/SJ caliber nightmare.

recent.text: They're not kicking any can down the road because they already began the process two and a half years ago. This was the entire point of what he was saying. Rebuilding has phases, and this season may begin a bottom-out phase, it may not. They're still rebuilding regardless.
recent.author: Kelsey Surmacz
recent.quoted_text: Nobody likes a rebuilding process, but it’s what the #Penguins have to do. They have been in no man’s land, the mushy middle - whatever you prefer to call it for too long now. No more kicking the can down the road. Get younger & potentially better.
